subject.title: Feature: config option to route gateway lifecycle warnings to a dedicated channel

question: Should OpenClaw add a general `messages` internal-warning destination/category router, and how should it interact with existing suppression and cron failure-destination controls?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix adds public config and changes warning-delivery semantics across gateway, agent, cron, and channel surfaces; automation cannot safely choose those product defaults.

options.title: Approve default-compatible router
options.body: Add an explicit opt-in router for lifecycle, tool-error, and system-notice warnings while preserving current active-channel behavior by default.

options.title: Keep suppression-only policy
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` and `cron.failureDestination` as the supported operator controls and narrow this issue to docs or channel-specific leaks.

options.title: Split by warning class
options.body: Defer a general router and handle lifecycle warnings, tool errors, and cron notifications as separate narrower issues.

recommendation.title: Approve default-compatible router
recommendation.body: Add an explicit opt-in router for lifecycle, tool-error, and system-notice warnings while preserving current active-channel behavior by default.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history on warning-policy behavior and merged adjacent fixes that deliberately left broader policy open.
